## Purpose

This notebook explores `Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_RasterPredictors.csv`, made by
`R_Code_Analysis/GHG_Raster_Extraction.R`. It has one row per site (48 sites),
with the mean and SD of 11 raster bands in 10, 30 and 50 m windows around each
chamber site. It also uses the climate variables in
`Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_Climate.csv`, made by
`Python_Code_Analysis/GHG_Climate_Extraction.ipynb`: ERA5-Land weather for the
14 days before each visit, and PRISM 1991–2020 normals. The notebook covers:

1. **Inter-correlations among predictors**, as a multicollinearity check. This
   includes whether the three window sizes add any distinct information, and
   how the climate variables relate to each other and to the raster predictors.
2. **Univariate relationships** between CH4 and CO2 flux and each raster and
   climate predictor.

Model fitting, and the spatial autocorrelation check on model residuals, will go
in a separate modeling notebook once we choose a model structure.

**Conventions**

* Flux is the site mean of the two sampling rounds (n = 48). Section 4.4 checks
  that each round on its own gives the same picture.
* **Spearman's ρ** is the main correlation statistic. CH4 is strongly
  right-skewed and has a few negative values. ρ works on ranks, so it does not
  need a transform and is robust to the few sites with very high flux.
* Plots show CH4 on a pseudo-log axis (`scales::pseudo_log_trans`, σ = 0.01).
  This axis is linear near zero, so negative fluxes still appear.
* p-values are descriptive. With n = 48, |ρ| ≳ 0.29 is p < 0.05 before any
  multiple-testing correction, and we run 66 tests per gas. The tables also
  report Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjusted values.

```{r setup}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(here)

## --- Settings ---------------------------------------------------------------
RASTER_CSV <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_RasterPredictors.csv")
CLIMATE_CSV <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_Climate.csv")
SITES_GPKG <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_all_site_data_GPSupd_6347.gpkg")

FOCAL_WINDOW <- 10 # window (m) used for the detailed single-window plots
COR_FLAG <- 0.7 # |rho| treated as "highly correlated"
VIF_FLAG <- 5 # VIF treated as problematic
CH4_SIGMA <- 0.01 # pseudo-log linear range for CH4 axes

## Band order from GHG_Raster_Extraction.R
BAND_ORDER <- c("DEM", "twi", "HAND", "CHM", "TPI", "DMV",
                "NDVI", "NDWI", "NDVI_lo", "NDWI_lo", "WETprob")

## Climate predictors (Python_Code_Analysis/GHG_Climate_Extraction.ipynb):
## column -> short label. anom_* are derived below.
CLIM_VARS <- c(
  era5_temperature_2m_14d          = "ERA5 Tmean 14d",
  era5_temperature_2m_max_14d      = "ERA5 Tmax 14d",
  era5_temperature_2m_min_14d      = "ERA5 Tmin 14d",
  era5_total_precipitation_sum_14d = "ERA5 Precip 14d",
  anom_tmean_14d                   = "Tmean anomaly 14d",
  anom_ppt_14d                     = "Precip anomaly 14d",
  prism_tmean_month                = "PRISM Tmean month",
  prism_tmax_month                 = "PRISM Tmax month",
  prism_tmin_month                 = "PRISM Tmin month",
  prism_ppt_month                  = "PRISM Precip month",
  prism_tmean_annual               = "PRISM Tmean annual",
  prism_tmax_annual                = "PRISM Tmax annual",
  prism_tmin_annual                = "PRISM Tmin annual",
  prism_ppt_annual                 = "PRISM Precip annual"
)
## Variables that change with the sampling date (vs. static annual normals)
CLIM_DATED <- names(CLIM_VARS)[!grepl("_annual$", names(CLIM_VARS))]

## --- Plot styling -----------------------------------------------------------
## Categorical slots 1-3 (validated for colorblind separation); wetland type
## also gets a shape so identity never relies on color alone.
WT_COLS <- c(EM = "#2a78d6", FO = "#eb6834", SS = "#1baf7a")
WT_SHAPES <- c(EM = 16, FO = 17, SS = 15)
DIV_LOW <- "#2a78d6"
DIV_MID <- "#f0efec"
DIV_HIGH <- "#e34948"

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      legend.position = "top"
    )
)

scale_fill_rho <- function(name = "Spearman ρ") {
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    name = name, low = DIV_LOW, mid = DIV_MID, high = DIV_HIGH,
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)
  )
}
scale_y_ch4 <- function(...) {
  scale_y_continuous(
    trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = CH4_SIGMA),
    breaks = c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10), ...
  )
}

## Spearman rho + p-value for two vectors
spearman <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
  ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x[ok], y[ok], method = "spearman", exact = FALSE))
  tibble(rho = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value, n = sum(ok))
}
```

## 1. Data

```{r load}
rast <- read.csv(RASTER_CSV, colClasses = c(huc12 = "character"))

flux_round <- st_read(SITES_GPKG, quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(Site_ID, Round_Number, Date, CH4_avg, CO2_avg)

flux_site <- flux_round |>
  group_by(Site_ID) |>
  summarise(
    CH4 = mean(CH4_avg),
    CO2 = mean(CO2_avg),
    n_rounds = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## Climate is per visit: ERA5 = 14 days before the sample date; PRISM month =
## 1991-2020 normal for the sample month. Anomalies compare the two (rough:
## ERA5 ~11 km vs PRISM ~800 m; monthly precip normal scaled to 14 days).
clim_round <- read.csv(CLIMATE_CSV) |>
  mutate(
    anom_tmean_14d = era5_temperature_2m_14d - prism_tmean_month,
    anom_ppt_14d = era5_total_precipitation_sum_14d - prism_ppt_month * 14 / 30.4
  ) |>
  select(Site_ID, Round_Number, all_of(names(CLIM_VARS)))

## Site mean of the two visits, matching the flux response
clim_site <- clim_round |>
  group_by(Site_ID) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(CLIM_VARS)), mean), .groups = "drop")

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(rast$Site_ID),
  setequal(rast$Site_ID, flux_site$Site_ID),
  setequal(clim_site$Site_ID, flux_site$Site_ID),
  !anyNA(clim_site)
)

dat <- rast |>
  left_join(flux_site, by = "Site_ID") |>
  left_join(clim_site, by = "Site_ID") |>
  mutate(
    Wetland_Type = factor(Wetland_Type, levels = names(WT_COLS)),
    Ecoregion = factor(Ecoregion)
  )

## Predictor columns: <BAND>_<mean|sd>_<W>m
pred_cols <- grep("_(mean|sd)_\\d+m$", names(rast), value = TRUE)

pred_info <- tibble(col = pred_cols) |>
  extract(col, c("band", "stat", "window"), "^(.*)_(mean|sd)_(\\d+)m$",
          remove = FALSE, convert = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    band = factor(band, levels = BAND_ORDER),
    stat = factor(stat, levels = c("mean", "sd")),
    feature = paste(band, stat, sep = "_")
  ) |>
  arrange(window, stat, band) |>
  mutate(feature = factor(feature, levels = unique(feature)))

clim_info <- tibble(col = names(CLIM_VARS), label = unname(CLIM_VARS)) |>
  mutate(
    source = case_when(
      startsWith(col, "era5") ~ "ERA5 14-day",
      startsWith(col, "anom") ~ "Anomaly (ERA5 - PRISM month)",
      endsWith(col, "_month") ~ "PRISM month normal",
      TRUE ~ "PRISM annual normal"
    ),
    label = factor(label, levels = label)
  )

cat(nrow(dat), "sites;", length(pred_cols), "raster predictors (",
    nlevels(pred_info$band), "bands x 2 stats x",
    n_distinct(pred_info$window), "windows );",
    nrow(clim_info), "climate predictors\n")
```

The extraction also writes diagnostic columns that are not predictors.

```{r diagnostics}
dat |>
  summarise(across(c(offset_m, starts_with("validfrac")),
                   list(min = min, median = median, max = max))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("column", ".value"),
               names_pattern = "^(.*)_(min|median|max)$") |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Extraction diagnostics")
```

`validfrac` is close to 1 everywhere, so no window loses a meaningful share of
pixels at a raster edge. `offset_m` (the distance from the point to its 10 m cell
centre) is at most about 6 m, which is small relative to the 30 and 50 m
windows.

### Predictor summaries

```{r pred-summary}
pred_summary <- dat |>
  select(all_of(pred_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "col") |>
  group_by(col) |>
  summarise(
    min = min(value), median = median(value), max = max(value),
    sd = sd(value), n_unique = n_distinct(round(value, 6)),
    prop_zero = mean(abs(value) < 1e-6),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(pred_info, by = "col") |>
  arrange(window, stat, band) |>
  select(col, min, median, max, sd, n_unique, prop_zero)

kable(pred_summary, digits = 3, caption = "Raster predictor summaries (n = 48)")

low_info <- filter(pred_summary, sd == 0 | n_unique < 10 | prop_zero > 0.5)
if (nrow(low_info)) {
  cat("Low-information predictors (constant, <10 unique values, or >50% zeros):\n",
      paste(low_info$col, collapse = ", "), "\n")
} else {
  cat("No constant or near-constant predictors.\n")
}
```

### Climate summaries

Climate values are site means of the two visits. The annual normals are
identical for both visits; the ERA5 and sample-month values differ by visit date.
ERA5-Land is about 11 km resolution, so sites close together can share a cell
(see `n_unique`).

```{r clim-summary}
dat |>
  select(all_of(clim_info$col)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "col") |>
  group_by(col) |>
  summarise(min = min(value), median = median(value), max = max(value),
            sd = sd(value), n_unique = n_distinct(round(value, 6)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  right_join(clim_info, by = "col") |>
  select(source, variable = label, min, median, max, sd, n_unique) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Climate predictor summaries (site means, n = 48; °C and mm)")
```

## 2. Response distributions

```{r round-consistency, fig.height=4}
flux_wide <- flux_round |>
  select(Site_ID, Round_Number, CH4_avg, CO2_avg) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Round_Number, values_from = c(CH4_avg, CO2_avg))

r_ch4 <- spearman(flux_wide$CH4_avg_1, flux_wide$CH4_avg_2)
r_co2 <- spearman(flux_wide$CO2_avg_1, flux_wide$CO2_avg_2)

p_ch4 <- ggplot(flux_wide, aes(CH4_avg_1, CH4_avg_2)) +
  geom_abline(color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = CH4_SIGMA),
                     breaks = c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10)) +
  scale_y_ch4() +
  labs(title = sprintf("CH4: round 1 vs round 2 (ρ = %.2f)", r_ch4$rho),
       x = "Round 1 CH4 flux", y = "Round 2 CH4 flux")

p_co2 <- ggplot(flux_wide, aes(CO2_avg_1, CO2_avg_2)) +
  geom_abline(color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = sprintf("CO2: round 1 vs round 2 (ρ = %.2f)", r_co2$rho),
       x = "Round 1 CO2 flux", y = "Round 2 CO2 flux")

p_ch4 + p_co2
```

The site mean of the two rounds is the response for the rest of this notebook.
If round-to-round agreement is weak, a mixed model with site as a random effect
(rounds as replicates) is a better choice for the modeling notebook than site
means.

```{r response-dist, fig.height=7}
h_ch4 <- ggplot(dat, aes(CH4)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#2a78d6", color = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = CH4_SIGMA),
                     breaks = c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10)) +
  labs(title = "Site-mean CH4 flux (pseudo-log axis)", x = NULL, y = "Sites")

h_co2 <- ggplot(dat, aes(CO2)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#2a78d6", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Site-mean CO2 flux", x = NULL, y = "Sites")

box_by <- function(group, gas, title) {
  p <- ggplot(dat, aes(.data[[group]], .data[[gas]])) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, color = "#898781", width = 0.5) +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type),
                width = 0.15, height = 0, size = 2.2, alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_color_manual(values = WT_COLS) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = WT_SHAPES) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = gas, color = "Wetland type", shape = "Wetland type")
  if (gas == "CH4") p <- p + scale_y_ch4()
  p
}

(h_ch4 + h_co2) /
  (box_by("Wetland_Type", "CH4", "CH4 by wetland type") +
     box_by("Wetland_Type", "CO2", "CO2 by wetland type")) /
  (box_by("Ecoregion", "CH4", "CH4 by ecoregion") +
     box_by("Ecoregion", "CO2", "CO2 by ecoregion")) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8))
```

Wetland type and ecoregion are candidate categorical terms or grouping factors
for the model. They provide context for the raster relationships below: a raster
predictor that only separates wetland types adds little once type is in the
model. Section 4.5 checks this.

## 3. Multicollinearity among raster predictors

### 3.1 Redundancy across window sizes

Does a band's 10, 30 and 50 m value carry distinct information? A high ρ between
windows means we can pick one window per band rather than enter several.

```{r cross-window, fig.height=5}
cross_window <- pred_info |>
  distinct(band, stat) |>
  mutate(pairs = map2(band, stat, function(b, s) {
    cols <- setNames(paste0(b, "_", s, "_", c(10, 30, 50), "m"), c(10, 30, 50))
    combn(names(cols), 2, simplify = FALSE) |>
      map_dfr(\(w) tibble(
        pair = paste0(w[1], " vs ", w[2], " m"),
        rho = cor(dat[[cols[w[1]]]], dat[[cols[w[2]]]], method = "spearman")
      ))
  })) |>
  unnest(pairs) |>
  mutate(pair = factor(pair, levels = c("10 vs 30 m", "30 vs 50 m", "10 vs 50 m")))

ggplot(cross_window, aes(pair, band, fill = rho)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", rho)), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~stat, labeller = labeller(stat = c(mean = "Window mean", sd = "Window SD"))) +
  scale_fill_rho() +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  labs(title = "Spearman ρ between window sizes, same band and statistic",
       x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

Means are usually close to redundant across windows, so window choice is mostly
a question of which scale best matches the flux signal (Section 4). SDs measure
within-window heterogeneity and change more with window size, since a larger
window takes in more of the surrounding landscape.

### 3.2 Correlation matrices within a window

Variables are ordered by hierarchical clustering on 1 − |ρ|, so blocks of
inter-correlated predictors sit together. Cells are labelled where
|ρ| ≥ `r COR_FLAG`.

```{r cor-fn}
cor_matrix <- function(w) {
  cols <- pred_info |> filter(window == w) |> arrange(stat, band)
  m <- cor(dat[cols$col], method = "spearman")
  dimnames(m) <- list(as.character(cols$feature), as.character(cols$feature))
  m
}

## Clustered heatmap of any square correlation matrix
plot_cor <- function(m, title) {
  ord <- hclust(as.dist(1 - abs(m)), method = "average")$order
  lv <- rownames(m)[ord]
  as_tibble(m, rownames = "x") |>
    pivot_longer(-x, names_to = "y", values_to = "rho") |>
    mutate(x = factor(x, levels = lv), y = factor(y, levels = rev(lv))) |>
    ggplot(aes(x, y, fill = rho)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(abs(rho) >= COR_FLAG & x != y,
                                 sprintf("%.2f", rho), "")),
              size = 2.4) +
    scale_fill_rho() +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
          panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
}

plot_cor_matrix <- function(w) {
  plot_cor(cor_matrix(w), sprintf("Predictor inter-correlation, %d m window", w))
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### 10 m

```{r cor-10, fig.height=8, fig.width=9}
plot_cor_matrix(10)
```

#### 30 m

```{r cor-30, fig.height=8, fig.width=9}
plot_cor_matrix(30)
```

#### 50 m

```{r cor-50, fig.height=8, fig.width=9}

```

### 3.3 Highly correlated pairs

```{r high-pairs}
high_pairs <- map_dfr(sort(unique(pred_info$window)), function(w) {
  m <- cor_matrix(w)
  idx <- which(upper.tri(m) & abs(m) >= COR_FLAG, arr.ind = TRUE)
  tibble(window_m = w, var1 = rownames(m)[idx[, 1]],
         var2 = colnames(m)[idx[, 2]], rho = m[idx])
}) |>
  arrange(window_m, desc(abs(rho)))

kable(high_pairs, digits = 2,
      caption = sprintf("Predictor pairs with |Spearman ρ| ≥ %.1f", COR_FLAG))
```

### 3.4 Predictor clusters

The cut at height 1 − `r COR_FLAG` groups predictors that are linked at
|ρ| ≥ `r COR_FLAG` on average. A sensible first model takes **one predictor from
each cluster**.

```{r clusters, fig.height=5}
m_focal <- cor_matrix(FOCAL_WINDOW)
hc <- hclust(as.dist(1 - abs(m_focal)), method = "average")
groups <- cutree(hc, h = 1 - COR_FLAG)

par(mar = c(1, 4, 3, 1))
plot(hc, main = sprintf("Predictor clustering (1 - |ρ|), %d m window", FOCAL_WINDOW),
     xlab = "", sub = "", ylab = "1 - |Spearman ρ|", cex = 0.8)
abline(h = 1 - COR_FLAG, lty = 2, col = DIV_HIGH)
rect.hclust(hc, h = 1 - COR_FLAG, border = "#898781")

tibble(cluster = groups, feature = names(groups)) |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  summarise(n = n(), members = paste(feature, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  kable(caption = sprintf("Clusters at |ρ| ≥ %.1f, %d m window", COR_FLAG, FOCAL_WINDOW))
```

### 3.5 Variance inflation factors

VIF depends only on the predictors (VIF~j~ = diagonal of the inverse correlation
matrix), so it can be checked before we choose a response or model form. With
n = 48, entering all 22 predictors of a window at once is not realistic anyway.
Instead, the table drops the highest-VIF predictor one at a time until every VIF
is below `r VIF_FLAG`. This shows how many predictors can sit together without
severe collinearity. It is a screening aid only. Final selection should weigh
ecological meaning and the flux relationships in Section 4.

```{r vif}
vif_of <- function(X) {
  r <- cor(X)
  v <- tryCatch(diag(solve(r)), error = function(e) rep(Inf, ncol(X)))
  setNames(v, colnames(X))
}

vif_stepdown <- function(X, thresh = VIF_FLAG) {
  dropped <- tibble(step = integer(), dropped = character(), vif = numeric())
  ## Columns that are exact linear combinations of earlier ones (VIF = Inf)
  ## are removed first; pivoted QR keeps the earlier column of each alias set.
  q <- qr(scale(X), tol = 1e-7)
  if (q$rank < ncol(X)) {
    aliased <- colnames(X)[q$pivot[-seq_len(q$rank)]]
    dropped <- add_row(dropped, step = seq_along(aliased),
                       dropped = paste(aliased, "(exact linear combination)"), vif = Inf)
    X <- X[, setdiff(colnames(X), aliased), drop = FALSE]
  }
  repeat {
    v <- vif_of(X)
    if (max(v) < thresh || ncol(X) <= 2) break
    worst <- names(which.max(v))
    dropped <- add_row(dropped, step = nrow(dropped) + 1L, dropped = worst, vif = max(v))
    X <- X[, setdiff(colnames(X), worst), drop = FALSE]
  }
  list(dropped = dropped, kept = tibble(feature = names(v), vif = unname(v)))
}

vif_res <- map(set_names(sort(unique(pred_info$window))), function(w) {
  cols <- pred_info |> filter(window == w) |> arrange(stat, band)
  X <- as.matrix(dat[cols$col])
  colnames(X) <- as.character(cols$feature)
  list(full = vif_of(X), step = vif_stepdown(X))
})

## Full-set VIFs, all windows side by side
imap_dfr(vif_res, \(r, w) tibble(window_m = w, feature = names(r$full), vif = r$full)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = window_m, values_from = vif, names_prefix = "VIF_") |>
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "VIF with all 22 predictors of a window entered together")
```

```{r vif-kept}
imap_dfr(vif_res, \(r, w) mutate(r$step$kept, window_m = w)) |>
  group_by(window_m) |>
  summarise(n_kept = n(),
            kept = paste(sprintf("%s (%.1f)", feature, vif), collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = sprintf("Predictors that remain after VIF step-down to < %d (VIF in brackets)", VIF_FLAG))
```

### 3.6 Climate predictors

**Among climate variables.** Within a product, the temperature variables
(mean, max, min) are expected to be close to redundant.

```{r clim-cor, fig.height=7, fig.width=8}
clim_X <- as.matrix(dat[clim_info$col])
colnames(clim_X) <- as.character(clim_info$label)
clim_m <- cor(clim_X, method = "spearman")
plot_cor(clim_m, "Climate predictor inter-correlation")
```

**Climate vs. raster predictors.** Climate varies smoothly over the state, and
so do some raster bands (for example, DEM). Where a climate variable and a
raster predictor are strongly correlated, they cannot be separated in a model.
The heatmap uses the `r FOCAL_WINDOW` m window; cells are labelled where
|ρ| ≥ `r COR_FLAG`.

```{r clim-rast-cor, fig.height=6, fig.width=10}
focal_info <- pred_info |> filter(window == FOCAL_WINDOW) |> arrange(stat, band)
rast_X <- as.matrix(dat[focal_info$col])
colnames(rast_X) <- as.character(focal_info$feature)

cross_m <- cor(clim_X, rast_X, method = "spearman")

as_tibble(cross_m, rownames = "climate") |>
  pivot_longer(-climate, names_to = "raster", values_to = "rho") |>
  mutate(climate = factor(climate, levels = rev(levels(clim_info$label))),
         raster = factor(raster, levels = colnames(rast_X))) |>
  ggplot(aes(raster, climate, fill = rho)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(abs(rho) >= COR_FLAG, sprintf("%.2f", rho), "")),
            size = 2.4) +
  scale_fill_rho() +
  labs(title = sprintf("Climate vs. raster predictors (%d m window)", FOCAL_WINDOW),
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
```

```{r clim-high-pairs}
clim_pairs <- bind_rows(
  {
    idx <- which(upper.tri(clim_m) & abs(clim_m) >= COR_FLAG, arr.ind = TRUE)
    tibble(type = "climate-climate", var1 = rownames(clim_m)[idx[, 1]],
           var2 = colnames(clim_m)[idx[, 2]], rho = clim_m[idx])
  },
  {
    idx <- which(abs(cross_m) >= COR_FLAG, arr.ind = TRUE)
    tibble(type = sprintf("climate-raster (%d m)", FOCAL_WINDOW),
           var1 = rownames(cross_m)[idx[, 1]],
           var2 = colnames(cross_m)[idx[, 2]], rho = cross_m[idx])
  }
) |>
  arrange(type, desc(abs(rho)))

kable(clim_pairs, digits = 2,
      caption = sprintf("Climate pairs with |Spearman ρ| ≥ %.1f", COR_FLAG))
```

**Joint VIF.** This starts from the raster predictors that remained after the
`r FOCAL_WINDOW` m VIF step-down (Section 3.5), adds all climate variables, and
repeats the step-down.

```{r clim-vif}
rast_kept <- vif_res[[as.character(FOCAL_WINDOW)]]$step$kept$feature
joint_step <- vif_stepdown(cbind(rast_X[, rast_kept, drop = FALSE], clim_X))

kable(joint_step$dropped, digits = 1,
      caption = "Dropped in order (VIF at the time of dropping)")
joint_step$kept |>
  mutate(type = ifelse(feature %in% clim_info$label, "climate", "raster")) |>
  arrange(type, desc(vif)) |>
  kable(digits = 1, caption = sprintf("Joint raster + climate set with all VIF < %d", VIF_FLAG))
```

## 4. Flux vs. raster predictors

### 4.1 Spearman correlations, all predictors and windows

```{r flux-cor}
flux_cor <- pred_info |>
  crossing(gas = c("CH4", "CO2")) |>
  mutate(res = map2(col, gas, \(p, g) spearman(dat[[p]], dat[[g]]))) |>
  unnest(res) |>
  group_by(gas) |>
  mutate(p_BH = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r flux-cor-heatmap, fig.height=7}
ggplot(flux_cor, aes(factor(window), band, fill = rho)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(p < 0.05, sprintf("%.2f", rho), "")), size = 3) +
  facet_grid(stat ~ gas, labeller = labeller(stat = c(mean = "Window mean", sd = "Window SD"))) +
  scale_fill_rho() +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  labs(title = "Spearman ρ between site-mean flux and raster predictors",
       subtitle = "Labels show cells with unadjusted p < 0.05",
       x = "Window (m)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

```{r flux-cor-table}
flux_cor |>
  group_by(gas) |>
  slice_max(abs(rho), n = 12) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(gas, predictor = col, rho, p, p_BH) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Strongest 12 predictors per gas by |Spearman ρ|")
```

### 4.2 Does window size matter?

```{r window-profile, fig.height=6}
ggplot(flux_cor, aes(window, rho, group = band)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-0.285, 0.285), color = "#c3c2b7", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(color = "#898781", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8, color = "#2a78d6") +
  facet_grid(gas + stat ~ band) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(10, 30, 50)) +
  labs(title = "Spearman ρ with flux across window sizes",
       subtitle = "Dashed lines are approximate unadjusted p = 0.05 for n = 48",
       x = "Window (m)", y = "ρ") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
```

### 4.3 Scatterplots at the `r FOCAL_WINDOW` m window

Each panel shows one predictor against site-mean flux. A grey LOESS line shows
the overall trend, and points are coloured and shaped by wetland type. The panel
title gives ρ.

```{r scatter-fn}
## Faceted scatterplots of flux vs. a set of columns; labels name each panel
scatter_grid <- function(gas, cols, labels, title) {
  rho_lab <- map_dfr(cols, \(p) spearman(dat[[p]], dat[[gas]])) |>
    mutate(col = cols,
           lab = sprintf("%s  (ρ = %.2f%s)", labels, rho, ifelse(p < 0.05, "*", "")))
  long <- dat |>
    select(Site_ID, Wetland_Type, y = all_of(gas), all_of(cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(all_of(cols), names_to = "col", values_to = "x") |>
    left_join(rho_lab, by = "col") |>
    mutate(lab = factor(lab, levels = rho_lab$lab))

  p <- ggplot(long, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, span = 1, se = FALSE,
                color = "#898781", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type), size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
    facet_wrap(~lab, scales = "free_x", ncol = 4) +
    scale_color_manual(values = WT_COLS) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = WT_SHAPES) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = "* unadjusted p < 0.05",
         x = NULL, y = paste("Site-mean", gas, "flux"),
         color = "Wetland type", shape = "Wetland type")
  if (gas == "CH4") p <- p + scale_y_ch4()
  p
}

scatter_panel <- function(gas, stat_sel, w = FOCAL_WINDOW) {
  cols <- pred_info |> filter(window == w, stat == stat_sel) |> arrange(band)
  scatter_grid(gas, cols$col, as.character(cols$band),
               sprintf("%s vs window %s predictors, %d m window", gas, stat_sel, w))
}
```

### 4.4 Consistency across sampling rounds

Are the site-mean correlations driven by one round? This recomputes ρ with each
round's flux separately at the focal window.

```{r round-rho, fig.height=6}
dat_round <- flux_round |>
  left_join(rast, by = "Site_ID")

focal_cols <- pred_info |> filter(window == FOCAL_WINDOW)

round_cor <- crossing(focal_cols, gas = c("CH4", "CO2"), round = c("1", "2")) |>
  mutate(res = pmap(list(col, gas, round), function(p, g, r) {
    d <- filter(dat_round, Round_Number == as.integer(r))
    spearman(d[[p]], d[[paste0(g, "_avg")]])
  })) |>
  unnest(res) |>
  bind_rows(
    flux_cor |> filter(window == FOCAL_WINDOW) |> mutate(round = "Site mean")
  ) |>
  mutate(round = factor(round, levels = c("1", "2", "Site mean"),
                        labels = c("Round 1", "Round 2", "Site mean")))

ggplot(round_cor, aes(rho, feature, color = round, shape = round)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~gas) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Round 1" = "#2a78d6", "Round 2" = "#eb6834",
                                "Site mean" = "#1baf7a")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17, 15)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Spearman ρ by sampling round, %d m window", FOCAL_WINDOW),
       x = "ρ", y = NULL, color = NULL, shape = NULL)
```

### 4.5 Within wetland type

If a predictor's correlation only reflects differences between wetland types,
the correlation within each type will be weak. Each type has only about 16
sites, so treat these values as rough indicators.

```{r within-type, fig.height=6}
top_feats <- flux_cor |>
  filter(window == FOCAL_WINDOW) |>
  group_by(gas) |>
  slice_max(abs(rho), n = 8) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(gas, col, feature)

within_cor <- top_feats |>
  crossing(Wetland_Type = c("All", levels(dat$Wetland_Type))) |>
  mutate(res = pmap(list(col, gas, Wetland_Type), function(p, g, t) {
    d <- if (t == "All") dat else filter(dat, Wetland_Type == t)
    spearman(d[[p]], d[[g]])
  })) |>
  unnest(res) |>
  mutate(Wetland_Type = factor(Wetland_Type, levels = c("All", names(WT_COLS))))

ggplot(within_cor, aes(rho, feature, color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~gas, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(All = "#0b0b0b", WT_COLS)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(All = 4, WT_SHAPES)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Top predictors: ρ overall and within wetland type (%d m)", FOCAL_WINDOW),
       x = "ρ", y = NULL, color = "Subset", shape = "Subset")
```

### 5.1 Spearman correlations

BH adjustment is applied within the 14 climate tests for each gas.

```{r clim-flux-cor, fig.height=5}

  crossing(gas = c("CH4", "CO2")) |>
  mutate(res = map2(col, gas, \(p, g) spearman(dat[[p]], dat[[g]]))) |>
  unnest(res) |>
  group_by(gas) |>
  mutate(p_BH = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(clim_flux_cor, aes(rho, label)) +

  geom_point(size = 2.6, color = "#2a78d6") +

       subtitle = "Dashed lines are approximate unadjusted p = 0.05 for n = 48",

clim_flux_cor |>
  select(gas, source, variable = label, rho, p, p_BH) |>
  arrange(gas, desc(abs(rho))) |>
```

### 5.3 Consistency across sampling rounds

The ERA5, anomaly and sample-month variables describe the conditions at each
visit, so here each round's flux is paired with that round's own climate values.
The annual normals are the same for both rounds.

```{r clim-round-rho, fig.height=5}
clim_flux_round <- flux_round |>
  left_join(clim_round, by = c("Site_ID", "Round_Number"))

clim_round_cor <- crossing(clim_info, gas = c("CH4", "CO2"), round = 1:2) |>
  mutate(res = pmap(list(col, gas, round), function(p, g, r) {
    d <- filter(clim_flux_round, Round_Number == r)
    spearman(d[[p]], d[[paste0(g, "_avg")]])
  })) |>
  unnest(res) |>
  mutate(round = as.character(round)) |>
  bind_rows(mutate(clim_flux_cor, round = "Site mean")) |>
  mutate(round = factor(round, levels = c("1", "2", "Site mean"),
                        labels = c("Round 1", "Round 2", "Site mean")))

ggplot(clim_round_cor, aes(rho, label, color = round, shape = round)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~gas) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Round 1" = "#2a78d6", "Round 2" = "#eb6834",
                                "Site mean" = "#1baf7a")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17, 15)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Spearman ρ with climate by sampling round",
       x = "ρ", y = NULL, color = NULL, shape = NULL)
```

```{r combined-rank}
bind_rows(
  flux_cor |> filter(window == FOCAL_WINDOW) |>
    transmute(gas, type = "raster", predictor = as.character(feature), rho, p),
  clim_flux_cor |>
    transmute(gas, type = "climate", predictor = as.character(label), rho, p)
) |>
  group_by(gas) |>
  slice_max(abs(rho), n = 10) |>
  ungroup() |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf(
    "Top 10 predictors per gas: raster (%d m window) and climate", FOCAL_WINDOW))
```

## 6. Notes for the modeling notebook

* **Window choice.** Use Section 3.1 together with Section 4.2. Where windows are
  redundant, pick the one with the strongest and most consistent flux signal. A
  single common window keeps the prediction map pipeline simple.
* **Climate.** The PRISM normals are static and could be mapped at prediction
  time. The ERA5 and anomaly variables describe the weather around each visit,
  so a statewide map needs a reference period (for example, a typical July).
  Section 3.6 shows which climate variables overlap with DEM or other raster
  predictors.
* **Predictor shortlist.** Take at most one predictor per cluster (Section 3.4).
  Section 3.5 shows how many can coexist with VIF < `r VIF_FLAG`. With n = 48,
  roughly 3–5 terms is a realistic ceiling for a regression model.
* **Response structure.** Choose between site means and round-level data with a
  site random effect (Section 2). Also decide how to handle CH4 skew and
  negative values, for example a Gamma or Tweedie GLM on shifted flux, a log or
  asinh transform, or rank-based / tree methods.
* **Spatial autocorrelation.** Check it on model residuals once a structure is
  chosen, for example with Moran's I or a variogram on residuals at the site
  coordinates (`x`, `y`, EPSG:6347), and with spatially blocked cross-validation
  (by HUC12 or cluster).
